castItem.roleDesc: recently come to Madrid to seek his fortune at court
his friend, and owner of the house in Madrid
a young widow, sister of Luis and Juan

div1.head: Act I

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Here we arrive in this magnificent city of Madrid, and miss the celebrations on the occasion of the baptism of the new prince by just one hour.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Such things happen, for good or ill, for want of an hour: If Pyramus had gone to the fountain an hour earlier he would not have found Thisbe dead or the mulberries turned purple with her blood. You know, the great poets say that the tragedy was written with mulberry juice. If Tarquin had not arrived an hour late, he would have found Lucretia safe and sound. (Of course, playwrights would not have gone from theater to theater trying to find out if she was raped or not.) If Hero had spent an hour thinking and deciding on the best thing to do, she would not have thrown herself from the tower, that’s for sure (in which case, no playwright would have had his greatest triumph writing her into his most famous play, and no actress would have chewed up the scenery playing her). Since we have missed the party by just one hour, let us not waste another before we find our destination. As the story goes, if one arrives late, he must remain outside the gate. Besides, I am dying to see this friend who is waiting for you as though you were a proper gentleman, without knowing how or why such good fortune has come to us. After all, even though we are not competitors in a tournament, it is he who supports us.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Don Juan de Toledo, Cosme, is the man whom I most dearly call friend. Our friendship rivals the great ones celebrated across the centuries. We studied together, then, passing from letters to arms, we were comrades together in war. In the Piedmont War, when the Duke of Feria made me a captain, I gave my flag to him. He was my lieutenant, Cosme, and suffered a deep wound in the fray; I cared for him in my own bed. He owes his life to me, second only to God. I have forgiven minor debts because it is unseemly to mention them among nobles. For that reason repayment of a favor is depicted as a rich woman with her back turned, meaning that once one has done something nice, discretion requires one to forget about it. Thus Juan, grateful for my friendship and my help, seeing that his Majesty has called me to court to reward my service, has invited me today to stay in his house. It is the least he could do. Although he wrote to me in Burgos, giving his address, I most certainly did not want to ask directions from his neighbors. That is why I left the mules and the baggage at the inn and came on foot to find his house. Then I saw the decorations and the finery and, when I found out the occasion, I hoped to see the celebration, if only by accident. But we arrived an hour too late....

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: If you are a gentleman, as your appearance would indicate you to be, please help a poor woman who must rely on your sense of duty. Honor and life itself are at stake. That gentleman must not know who I am. I pray you, prevent him from following me. Upon your life, rescue a lady from certain misfortune and dishonor. It might be that one day.... [She starts to leave.] Good-bye! I am undone.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Was that a lady or a whirlwind?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: What a turn of events!

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: What do you plan to do?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: You need to ask? How could my nobility fail to come to her aid and prevent her misfortune and her dishonor? The man must surely be her husband.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: What are you thinking?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: I shall detain him by some trick. Of course, if that is to no avail, I shall have to resort to force even though I may have to invent an excuse.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: If you are looking for a trick, wait... I think I have something here. This letter of introduction from a friend should do.

div1.stage: Enter Luis and Rodrigo, his servant.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: I have to meet her, if only because she goes to such lengths to avoid me.

sp.speaker: Rodrigo
sp.p: Follow her and you will know who she is.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Sir, although I am embarrassed to approach you, might your worship please do me a great favor and read me this letter.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: I am in too much of a hurry. I have no time for such things.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Well, if you need a little, I have plenty for both of us.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: Leave me alone.

p.seg: (This street is entirely too straight; they are still in sight.)

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: I beseech you, Sir.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: Good God, you are irritating. I shall thrash you soundly if you do me much....

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: For that reason, I’ll just do you a little.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: I have no more patience for you. Get away!

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p:
(Aside) (I must intervene. Let valor finish what caution began.) [He approaches Luis.]
Sir, this servant is mine, and I do not know how he must have offended you for you to mistreat him so.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: I do not respond to those who doubt or complain about my actions. Good day.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: You may be quite certain that if I required satisfaction, I should not leave without it, despite your arrogance. My asking how he has offended you, so that I may punish him for his error, deserves more courtesy. Since courtly manners demand it, please do not disparage it, even when a stranger should come to teach it to you who have the obligation, as nobles at court, to know it.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: Who dares think that I lack courtesy?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Silence your tongue; let your sword speak.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: You speak well.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Good God! They’re going to fight!.

sp.speaker: Rodrigo
sp.p: [To Cosme] Draw your sword.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Oh, no! It’s a virgin. Without express permission, it’s not allowed to show its face.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: Let go, Beatriz.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: You must not go.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: But the fight is with my brother.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: Oh, wretched fortune.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: I am here to help.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: Juan, wait. Rather than helping me, you are making me look like a coward. This stranger needs no help; he even has a servant. Please go, for God’s sake. As a nobleman, I can do my own fighting, and even more so with an adversary of such skill and grace. Now please leave.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: I am taken by your charm and gentle manner. But if you still have the slightest quarrel with me, I shall meet you at your convenience.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: Agreed.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Agreed.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: I cannot believe my eyes and ears. Manuel!

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Juan!

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: My soul is in turmoil and cannot decide what to do. My brother and my friend, which is the same thing, ready to fight? I cannot believe it. I must know the cause.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: Then listen: This gentlemen intervened on behalf of his servant, a fool who provoked me to speak harshly to him. This is the result.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: Since that is all it is, please allow me to welcome our guest with a warm embrace. This gentleman is Manuel, the houseguest we have been expecting. Luis, I want you two, who have demonstrated equal valor, to be friends. Shake hands.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Before I do, because I have witnessed his courage and skill, I am bound by honor to offer my service to Luis.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: I consider myself your friend, and lament that I did not recognize you. Your valor should have been enough to identify you.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Yours leaves mine humiliated. See? You have wounded my hand.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: A thousand times over do I wish the wound were mine!

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: What a courteous fight!

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: Wound? Come, we shall have it bandaged. Luis, you stay here and see Beatriz to her carriage. You can give her our apology. Come, Manuel, to my house, which is also your house, where you may get treatment.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: But it is nothing.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: Come along.

p.seg: How sad that Madrid should receive me thus with blood!
How sad that I was unable to find out who that woman was!

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: How nice that things turned out well for my master, unlike Don Quixote when he tried to save a maiden!

div1.stage: (Exeunt Manuel, Juan and Cosme. Luis approaches Beatriz, who is standing off to one side.)

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: The storm has passed. Once again, madam, allow me to restore to bloom the flower of your beauty that an accident has caused to wither.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: Where is Juan?

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: He asks your forgiveness, but necessary obligations have called him away, as well as the desire to care for the health of an injured friend.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: Oh my! I am undone! Is Juan injured?

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: Madam, it is not Juan. I could not possibly remain here so calmly if my brother were wounded. Be not afraid; it is not right, since he is not injured, that between the two of us you should suffer and I should be in pain. I say in pain because I see you so captivated by an imagined ill and it hurts me all the more.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: My dear Luis, you know how much I appreciate your attentions; I know they are heartfelt and sincere. But I cannot repay them. Only fate can alter love and it suffers no entreaties. If what is most scarce is today most cherished at court, hold in esteem the truth, for it is indeed a rare commodity.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p:
Go in peace. [Exit Beatriz with her maid.]
There is nothing, Rodrigo, that turns out well for me. If I see a well-born lady and wish to meet her, a fool and a fight interrupt me. I do not know which is worse, for if I fight, my brother arrives and my enemy is his friend. If my brother leaves his lady in my keeping, she rejects my sincere overtures. A veiled lady flees from me, a fool torments me, a stranger wants to kill me, a brother brings him home as a guest in our house, and another lady spurns me. Things couldn’t get much worse.

sp.speaker: Rodrigo
sp.p: I think I know which of all your woes troubles you most.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: How could you know?

sp.speaker: Rodrigo
sp.p: The one you feel most strongly is your jealousy of your brother and the beautiful Beatriz.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: You are quite mistaken.

sp.speaker: Rodrigo
sp.p: Then what is it?

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: If I speak truthfully, and I feel I can trust only you, what causes me most alarm is that my brother casually invites a handsome young man to our house, knowing that in it there is also our sister, a young widow, as you know, who lives so cloistered that the sun scarcely knows where she lives. Beatriz is the only person who visits her.

sp.speaker: Rodrigo
sp.p: I know that her husband was a port administrator with a modest salary, and that he died owing the crown a tidy sum, and that she came to court in secret to see to his affairs in private. This excuses your brother. If you consider that as a widow no one is allowed to visit her, and even though your guest is Manuel, no one is to know that such a woman is imprisoned in your house, what harm can come from having him there? Especially since, as a result of considerable care and thought, the door to his room opens directly onto the street. The old door to the rest of the house has been closed up, and in front of it has been placed a cupboard with mirrored doors designed in such a way that no one would suspect that there is a passageway behind it. In this way you all suspicion is removed with the door closed, yet it still allows one to be able to open it again.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: You think this gives me a sense of security? The very fact fills me with dread. What you are telling me is that nothing stands in defense of Angela’s honor except a few mirrored panes of glass, which can easily broken with one blow.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Isabel, hand me that scarf. What a miserable life! I must live in a shroud, dead to the world as a result of my enormous misfortune.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Take it quickly. If your brother should come and have the slightest suspicion, at least your appearance should not give you away. He must not see you dressed as you were at court this morning.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: God help me! I am dying entombed by these four walls. The sun hardly knows of my existence. But my woes can be neither contained nor cured in the course of a single day. Even the inconstant moon, who learns her fickleness from me, cannot say that she has seen me weeping in misery. In effect, I have lived my life in a cage, completely without freedom, only because I was widowed by a husband and now as good as married to two brothers. That it should be a crime to leave this house, to go where people are, where there are plays and gossip and important events! Just to walk about the streets in disguise, causing no dishonor, flouting no authority! Oh cruel stars! Oh wretched fortune!

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Madam, there is no doubt that your zealous brothers are concerned for your well-being. You are, after all, a widow, young, beautiful, and intelligent. Your status is the one that leads to the most problems with love. Even more so today, when men at court frequently entertain their perfumed “widows”! My God! When I see perfumed hussies gallivanting around town pretending to be so virtuous, so saintly, so modest, so circumspect. All they really care about is showing off their new dresses. Take away their finery and pious gestures and they become as flighty as a ball of paper on the wind, talking to all the young men they meet. But let us leave this discussion for another time. How is it we have not mentioned the stranger who came to the rescue of your honor, the one who presented himself today as your savior?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: You have read my soul by speaking of him. The thought of him has me quite unnerved, not on his account but on mine. Afterwards, when I heard the sound of knives, I thought — and these are just fantasies, Isabel — that he might take my misery so much to heart that he would draw his sword in my defense. I was foolish to implicate him in such a fashion, but a woman in turmoil, what is she to think or do?

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: I do not know if he stopped him; I only know that your brother followed us no more.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Wait, listen!

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: Angela!

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Dear brother! What brings you here in such a state? What has happened? What is wrong?

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: A terrible burden, a question of honor.

p.seg: Oh no! Doubtlessly Luis recognized me!

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: And I am most worried that our honor is in danger.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Has someone caused you to feel uneasy?

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: How strange! Here in your presence, Angela, I feel that same uneasy feeling as before.

p.seg: Another shock?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: But Luis, how can I cause you displeasure? You know....

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: You are the cause. Seeing you....

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Oh my!

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: Angela, our brother has so little esteem for you...

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: That must be it!

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: ...that he heaps new troubles on top of those that brought you here. I was right to turn the anger I feel for our brother against our guest. Without recognizing him, I wounded him prophetically.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Do tell.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: I went to the Palace Square on foot. It was full of coaches and gentlemen. I went over to a group of friends who were happily enthralled talking to a veiled lady. They all celebrated her wit and praised her intelligence and humor. From the moment I arrived, she spoke not a word. One gentleman even asked her why she fell silent when I joined the group. Her actions made me most uncomfortable. I looked to see if I knew her, but I could not make out her face. She wrapped her veil more tightly around her to hide her identity and protect herself. Because I could not see her face, I was determined to follow her. As she walked, she kept turning around to see if I was behind her. Her nervousness piqued my interest all the more. We were walking along in this manner when a man, the servant of our guest, stopped me so that I might read a letter for him. I answered that I was in a great hurry. I believe he stopped me on purpose because I saw the lady speak to him in passing. He was so insistent. I said something or other to him and our guest, looking all menacing and military, came to his defense. To make a long story short, we drew swords, but that is all. It could have been much worse.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: What an evil woman to have put you in such a situation! Oh, these conniving women! I should assume that she did not know who you were, and that she only did what she did because you were following her. I have told you repeatedly, if you will remember, that you should not go chasing after these silly women who know only how to cause the ruin of men.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: What have you been doing this afternoon?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: I have been here, at home, passing the hours weeping.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: Have you seen our brother?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: He has not been here since this morning.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: I simply cannot tolerate his inattention.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Think no more of it. Sometimes it is best to suffer in silence. He is our older brother, and we live off his fortune.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: Well, if you are not upset, then neither am I. I was only worried about you. Since you think that he and I can mend our friendship, I shall go see him and perhaps even engage in some diversion with him.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: In light of this cruel shock, my lady, what have you to say about what is going on in our own house? The one who defended your life today is now a wounded guest in your home?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: I suspected as much, Isabel, when I heard my brother’s account of the incident and when I saw that our guest was wounded. But I could not bring myself to believe it. What an extraordinary coincidence that a man should come to Madrid, that a woman should immediately ask him to defend her life, that one brother should wound him and another should give him shelter. This is all too much! Although it may be true, I shall not believe it until I see it with my own eyes.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: If you are determined to discover the truth, I know how you can see him, and even more, if you wish.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: You are mad. How, if his room is so far from my own?

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: There is a way to get from one room to the other. Do not be alarmed.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Not because I want to see him, but only because I am just generally curious, tell me, how? I hear you, but I do not believe you.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Have you not heard that your brother had a cupboard built over the door?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: I think I understand your plan. You want us to make a hole in a plank of the cupboard so that we can see into his room?

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Oh, it’s much better than that.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Go on.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Your brother closed up and covered over the door that was here and that led to the garden, but he also wanted a way to be able to open the door again at a later time. He had built a movable cupboard. Even though it is covered with mirrors, it slides open and shut quite easily. I know it well because once I was cleaning the cupboard and had placed a ladder against it. It started moving under my weight little by little until we all fell: me, the ladder, and the cupboard. I left the cupboard in such a state that, by moving it, anyone can pass through the door.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Before I prove the truth of your words, I need to know more. If I want to go to the other room, and have moved the cupboard, can it be moved from the other side as well?

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Of course. What makes it even better is that I have set two nails that are easy to remove, but only those who know to remove them can move the cupboard.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Tell the servant who brings him candles and linens to let you know if and when our guest leaves the house. If I am right, his wound will not require him to stay in bed.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: My God! Will you actually go?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: I have a foolish desire to know if he is the one who saved my life. If I have caused him concern and he has even spilled his blood for me, Isabel, it is right that I see after his wound. I hope to return the favor, but I must be certain that I shall not be found out. Let us go; I want to see this cupboard. If I can pass from one room to the other, I shall take care, without his realizing it, to repay his kindness.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: This is going to be an adventure! What if he figures it out?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: He will not. A man whose strength I assume to be equal to his nobility and discretion since he proved his worth to me in my first meeting with him, a man who is valiant and daring, bold and gallant, a man so richly endowed is not going to cause me to reveal my secret. It would be a notable waste for such a noble man to tell all he knows to anyone who passes by.

div1.stage: (Enter Juan, Manuel and a servant with a candle.)

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: Get some rest, for God’s sake.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: This wound is nothing, Juan. Honestly, it is unseemly for me to pay it any mind at all.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: I thank my stars that it is nothing worse than that, for I could never be consoled if my happiness in seeing you came at the cost of having you indisposed in my house and seeing you with your hand wounded, not by me, but by my brother.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: He is a worthy gentleman. I am envious of his ability with a sword and his noble style, and I hope to be a good friend to him and his servant.

div1.stage: (Enter Luis and a servant with a covered basked with a sheathed sword inside.)

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: Sir, I am your humble servant, and I hope to demonstrate the pain I feel by dedicating my life to you. So that the instrument that caused your wound not remain in my power, since it can no longer serve me nor please me, I shall send it from me much as one would an unworthy servant who causes his master some displeasure. This, Sir, is the sword that wounded you. I offer it to you and ask you to forgive it, if it is at all blameworthy. With it, take your revenge against me and against it.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: You are most noble and discreet; I am won over. I accept the sword so that it may show me how to be valiant. I intend to live confident from this day forward, for who would not feel safe with your sword at his side? Of it alone was I afraid.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: Since Luis has showed me how to treat a guest properly, I hope you will receive another gift from me.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: I can never hope to repay such generosity. You seem to be competing to shower me with honor.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: May two hundred thousand demons give testimony of their infernal fury and turn against me two hundred thousand snakes who might seize me and send me on my way to the great beyond if I would not rather live in peace in Galicia or Asturias than in this city and this court.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: What?

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Porter reporting for duty.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: What are you talking about?

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Just what I said. The one who gives passage to his enemy is a traitor.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: What enemy? Wait.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: The water from one fountain or another.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Water upsets you?

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Here I am, lost beneath this mountain of baggage, when of course I trip against the foot of a fountain and end up filthy. These things are not fit to bring indoors.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Get out of here, you’re drunk.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: If I were drunk, I wouldn’t be so angry at the water. I read in a book that fountains sometimes have their water transformed into other things. It wouldn’t be so bad to see a fountain have its water turned into wine.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: If he gets started, he will not finish in a year.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: He has an odd sense of humor.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: I would like to know something. If you can read, since you mentioned a book, why did you stop me at such an inopportune moment to read a letter?

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Well, I know how to read from books, but not from letters.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: What an answer!

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Please pay him no mind, for the love of God. You will come to know him and see that he is a joker.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: I hope to make my jokes famous. You are welcome to them.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: If it is not too late, I should like to pay a visit, one of some importance to me.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: I hope to see you again for dinner.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Cosme, don’t get anything dirty with the mud from that baggage when you open it and take out my clothing.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Good grief!

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: If you wish to lock your room, here is the key. I have a master key because I frequently come home late, after two, but you may be sure that this is the only key and that there is no other door. If you leave it in the lock, the servants will come daily to clean.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p:
Where are you, my little fortune? I want to see you first of all and determine how much we have pilfered along the way. People in roadside inns do not look after every little thing as carefully as they do in private houses. There is a greater opportunity for benefit by putting my hand, not on my heart, but in another’s purse. (He opens a suitcase and pulls out a purse.)
Here it is! Safe and sound. Just this morning it was a maiden and now, look, it’s quite pregnant. Let’s have a count. No, that’s not necessary. After all, it’s not as though I have just sold my master some sheep and need to figure the amount down to the last coin. What I have is what I have. Well, then. His suitcase is over there. I need to take out clothes in case he goes to bed soon. He ordered me to do that, but just because he ordered it, do I have to do it quickly? Just because he ordered it doesn’t mean I have to do it at all, for I am a servant. I could just as easily go out to a local tavern for a bit. Would you like that, Cosme? Why yes! Then let’s go, because our wishes come before our masters’.

div1.stage: (Exit. The cupboard moves and from behind it emerge Angela and Isabel.)

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Rodrigo said the room was empty; the guest and your brothers left.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: I would have done this just to have this adventure!

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: You see that there is no trouble getting from one room to the other.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: All the troubles I envisioned, Isabel, were groundless. We met no resistance at all. The door opens and closes easily and no one is the wiser.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Why have we come?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Just to have a look and come right back. For two women to create some mischief they only have to think about it. We are here just because we happened to speak of it a couple of times. I am determined, if in fact this gentleman is the one who risked his personal safety for me, to repay his attention.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Here is the gift your brother gave him, and a sword on a desk.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Come here. They brought my writing desk here?

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Yes. They thought he might like to write a message, or read a book.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: There are two suitcases on the floor.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Open, too! Shall we see what is in them?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Yes. It is foolish, but I want to see what clothing and other finery he has.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: He’s a soldier and a pretender at court. I doubt he has much to look at.

div1.stage: (They take the things out of the suitcases as they talk about them, and strew them about the room)

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: What’s this?

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Sheets of paper.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: From a woman?

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: No, madam. Just bound documents. They are quite heavy.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Well, if they were from a woman, they would be more lightweight. Do not waste your time on them.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: There is some underwear.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Does it smell good?

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Yes, it smells clean.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: That is the best perfume.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: It has all three qualities: thin, white, and soft. Madam, what is this leather case full of various instruments?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Let me see. This thing looks like dentist’s pliers. These are tweezers, that is a curling iron for his hair and here is another one for his moustache.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Here is a brush and comb. This man comes prepared. I wouldn’t be surprised to find shoe trees!

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Why?

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Because here they are.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Is there more?

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Yes, my lady, a second pouch full of letters.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Let me see. These are from a woman, and there is more than letters. Here is a portrait!

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: That fascinates you?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Just seeing beauty, even painted, is a pleasure.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: It seems that finding it has troubled you.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: How foolish you are. Look no further.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: What are you thinking?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: I shall leave him a note. Take this portrait.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Meanwhile, I’m going to check out the servant’s bag. This is money: coins, but of little value. In a world where doubloons are king, these are peasants. I think I’ll play a little trick. I’m going to take the lackey’s money and leave in its place some coals. You may wonder where I’ll get coals, but remember, this is winter and there is a brazier in the room.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: There! All done! Where should I leave this letter so that our guest will find it but my brother will not?

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Here, underneath the bedspread. When he turns it down, he cannot help but find it, but no one else will see it.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Good idea! Put it there and pick these things up.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Look! They are turning the lock!

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Leave all this, then. We must hide. Come, Isabel.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: May the cupboard protect me!

div1.stage: (Exeunt through the cupboard, which appears as it did at first. Enter Cosme.)

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Now that I have taken care of myself I am more of a mind to do my master’s bidding—and I won’t even charge him extra! But wait! Who has been in our room tossing our things about? Christ's blood! Our nice little room with our nice little possessions… now it all looks like a Turkish bazaar! Who is here? There is no one, by God, or if there is someone, he does not wish to answer. Fine. Don’t answer me. I am proud to say I don’t much care for talkers. Whatever it may be, to tell the truth, I am trembling like a leaf. On the other hand, if the intruder leaves me my money, let him make his mischief a thousand times a thousand. But what’s this? God’s wounds! My money converted into coals? Here now, little spirit! Whoever you were and are, turn your money into anything you desire, but the money I steal... why?

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: Why are you shouting?

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: What’s wrong?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: What has happened? Speak!

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: A pretty situation this! Why did you invite us to stay here in a room already occupied by a ghost? I was absent for just a second, and I returned to discover the clothing as you see it, strewn about. It looks like a clearance sale!

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: Is anything missing?

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Nothing. Just the money that I had in this purse. It was mine, and now it has been turned into coals.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: I see. This is another one of your jokes.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: What a cold and graceless deception.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: How evil and impertinent.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: It is no joke. For the love of God.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Quiet. This is so like you.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: That’s true, although I am also accustomed to being sane from time to time.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: I’ll take my leave, Manuel. Have a good night, and may the spirit of the house watch over you. And do advise your servant that we expect more of his wit in the future.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: It is not for nothing that you are as valiant as you are if you have to spend all your waking moments solving the disputes and problems created by this fool.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: You see how they treat me because of you? Everyone thinks me a madman because I put up with you. Wherever I go, a thousand misfortunes befall me on your account.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: We are now alone; there is no reason to deceive you. You cannot finesse a card trick with only two players. May two thousand devils take me if it is not true that when I left, someone or something entered and created this mess.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: You just want me to forgive you. Pick up these things you have strewn about and get ready for bed.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Sir, may I end up a galley slave....

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Enough! Hush, or, as God is my witness, I’ll break your head open!

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: It’s bad enough that I should have gone through such a trauma, but now I have to put back everything in these suitcases. Good heavens! May my money come back from the dead just as it will on Judgment Day!

div1.stage: (Manuel returns with a sheet of paper.)

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: A light, Cosme.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: What is it, sir? Have you perhaps discovered someone else in the house?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: I went to get ready for bed, Cosme, and I discovered under my bedspread this sealed note. The address on the envelope has me fascinated.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Who is it for?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Me, but the strange manner of its words has me entranced.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: What does it say?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: (Reads.) “Let no one open me, for I belong only to Manuel.”

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: God Almighty! And you didn’t believe me! Do not open it, I beseech you, without first exorcising its evil.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Cosme, what has me transfixed is its novelty, not its fearfulness. He who admires something cannot fear it. (Reads.) “Your well-being has me preoccupied, since I was the cause of your misfortune. Appreciative but worried, I beseech you to tell me how you are and to call on me. There will be occasion for both if you leave your answer where you found this note. Be warned that secrecy is paramount, because the day that one of your friends discovers this, my life and my honor will be forfeit.”

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: How strange!

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Strange?

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: You don’t find this strange?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Not at all. This actually clears up a few mysteries.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: How?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: It is quite clear that the veiled lady who was fleeing Luis so blindly and so desperately, was his lady, Cosme. She cannot be his wife because he is unmarried. And since this is quite certain, how difficult is it to imagine that his lady should have access to her beloved’s house?

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: That’s all very well and good, but it doesn’t calm my nerves. Let’s say she is his lady and the encounter happened as you say. But how was she able, from her position on the sidewalk, to know what was going to happen in order to have this note prepared and waiting for you on your bed?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: After our meeting, she could have given it to a servant.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Even if she had done that, how did a servant get in here to place it? No one entered the entire time I was in here.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: It could have happened earlier.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Of course. But finding the suitcases and our clothing cast about here and there, not to mention the note, leads me to suspect something more.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: See if the windows are locked.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Locked, and with iron grates on the outside.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: You leave me with greater doubts and a thousand suspicions.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: What about?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: I do not know how to explain them.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: And now, what are you to do?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: I intend to write an answer to this note in order to find out the truth of the situation. I shall use a style that conceals any astonishment or fear on my part. I have no doubt, since paper is involved, that we shall have occasion to see who brings it and takes it away.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: And should we not tell our hosts?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: No. I do not wish to cause the slightest problem for this woman, since she trusted her honor to me.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Then you prefer to dishonor the man you consider to be her beloved?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: No, not that either. Without causing her any problem I can still carry out my plan.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: No, sir. There is more here than you know of, and every moment my suspicion grows.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: How so?

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: You see that papers come and go around here with no visible way in or out. How do you suppose that happens?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: There exists some trick or artifice for entering and leaving, for opening and closing, somewhere in the room. I may lose my mind if I do not figure out how this happens, Cosme, but I shall never believe it is a supernatural phenomenon.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Are there no spirits?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: No one has seen them.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Ghosts?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Just fantasies.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Witches?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Hardly.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Demons?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Please.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Imps?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Enchantresses?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Neither.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Magicians?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Foolishness.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Necromancers?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Ridiculous.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Sorceresses?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: What madness.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: I know, by God, now I’ve got you! Devils?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Not that I know of.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Are there souls in purgatory?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: That fall in love with me? Is there greater lunacy? Leave me alone; I am tired.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: So, what have you decided?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: To be attentive, day and night; to be exceedingly cautious. I base my discovery of the truth on this. There is no need to resort to spirits or sorceresses.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Well, I do assume that some demon is involved. And it appears that he can come and go, bring things and take them, all in a puff of smoke.

div1.head: Act II

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: What extraordinary tales!

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: You have not even heard the most remarkable part! Where were we?

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: You had just passed through the cupboard into their room. It is difficult to imagine that it was so easy to open the cupboard, write him a note, and find the answer the following day.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: I tell you honestly, I have never seen such a courtly and gallant style, mixing the humorous with the astonishing, imitating knights errant to whom such adventures were commonplace. This, Beatriz, is the letter. I hope you like it. (Reads.) “Most beauteous damsel, in whatever way you may have been aggrieved by this, your faithful servant, may you lessen his hardships by your ample piety. Pray make known to me the identity of the evil malefactor or pagan conjurer who imprisons you in this enchantment, such that, now that my earlier wounds have healed, I might present myself as your defender in single and terrible combat, even though I may perish in the pursuit. Life is no better than death, if a knight have not honor. May the giver of light hold you safe and forget me not. The Knight of the Phantom Lady.”

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: My heavens! What a style, with the language of enchantment and adventure!

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: I waited for this note with the greatest fear and doubt, but when I found in him a willingness to proceed, I decided to continue in the same fashion. By way of answer, I sent...

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: Wait, go no further. Your brother Juan is coming.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: He comes no doubt to express his pleasure at your visit, Beatriz. As a faithful suitor, he welcomes you to his house.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: I am not unhappy about that, if truth be told.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: Every cloud has a silver lining, according to the old adage. In this case it is quite true, for the clouds of your troubles have given rise to a silver lining for me. Lovely Beatriz, I have discovered that a problem that you have with your father has brought you, without joy or pleasure, to our house. I deeply regret that my happiness in seeing you should come at the expense of your ill fortune. It is not right that I should be so elated because of your misery. But love today produces various effects: unhappiness for you, ecstasy for me. It’s just like the snake that has not only venom but also the antidote to treat it. You are most welcome here. Although your stay may be short, it’s always a joy to see the sun accompanied by an angel.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: You have so thoroughly confused your welcome with your regrets that I know not how to respond. It is true I come because of my father. You were to blame. Although he does not know it was you, he does know that I spoke with someone from the balcony last night. While he gets over his rage, he wishes me to spend time with my cousin, taking refuge in the great confidence he has in her. This alone shall I tell you; let this suffice. I, too, can find good in ill. Love causes contradictory effects in me as well. Just as the sun, when it sends forth its beautiful rays, causes one flower to bloom and another to wither, so too does love wound my heart at the same time that I most happy to find myself in your house, which has always been like a glittering diamond, outshining the sun, a worthy setting for an angel.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: How clearly one sees the riches you two take from love. By merely standing near you, I too receive a windfall of affection.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: Do you know what I think, Angela? Just to avenge the problems that my houseguest has caused you, you cunningly invited a houseguest of your own, one sure to cause me no end of grief.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: You speak truly, but I have done so only so that you may shower her with gifts.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: I am exceedingly pleased with your punishment.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: What are you doing, Juan? Where are you going?

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: Beatriz, to serve you. Only the obligation to serve you could make me leave.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Let him go.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: Until we meet again.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: If he thinks he caused me troubles with his houseguest, he is quite right. But they will be no less than the troubles he creates for himself because of you. I hope to use our guest to take away all our troubles. That way, guest for guest, we shall be even.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: I still want to know more about your guest!

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: To make a long story short, notes, both mine and his, came and went. His were so remarkable, I’ve never seen such a hodgepodge of truth and lies.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: And in the end, what does he make of the situation?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: He believes that I must be Luis’s lady since I was hiding from him but I have the key to his house.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: There is only one more problem I see.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: What is that?

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: How is it possible that this gentleman, seeing that someone is bringing and taking away papers, has not spied you or, worse, caught you red-handed?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: That is not so hard to explain. At the door to his room I station a servant who lets me know who enters and who leaves. Thus, Isabel does not go through the cupboard until I know that no one is in the room. That poor servant has spent an entire day watching, all in vain. Oh! But while I’m thinking of Isabel, would you mind taking her this basket. It’s just about time.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: One more doubt: How is it possible that you praise this gentleman as so intelligent when he has not been able to figure out the secret of the cupboard?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Surely you’ve heard of the egg, that more than one genius tried to stand on its end, and along came a simple man who gave it just one tap and it stood right up? The greatest problems are just that until they are solved. If one knows the trick, everything is easy.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: Another question.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: What?

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: What do you hope to gain by such tomfoolery?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: I’m not sure. I should say I would like to appear grateful for his help, but unfortunately I have become a bit jealous of a portrait of a lady that he has with him. I am of a mind to enter and seize it at the first opportunity. I know not how else to say that I am determined to enter so that he may see me and speak to me.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: And recognize you for who you are?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: May the saints protect me! I should say not! A friend would not commit such treason to a guest. Just the thought that I am his host’s lady makes his writing to me timid, courtly, confused, and cowardly. I certainly do not wish to make the situation worse.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: Then how is he to see you?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Listen, and I shall tell you the most astonishing plan by which I run no risk of being caught in his room. He will come here, but he will not know how.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Add another brother to the mix. Here comes Luis.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: I’ll tell you later.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: How fickle are the fortunes of love! How curious that heaven should in equal measure throw up such obstacles. The same desire pleases one and annoys the other. Let us go. I do not want Luis to speak to me here.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: Why are you leaving?

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: Because you entered.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: The most beautiful, the purest light ever captured from the sun flees because I enter? Am I the dark of night? May your beauty forgive me if I tarry here, bold and discourteous, to beseech a favor from you that you will not grant. Knowing of your cruelty, my desire cannot hope that even the smallest courtesy may be well received. I realize that my foolish love finds not one atom of hope in your disdain. But in the face of such rejection, I must persist in loving you. You shall give me greater glory, even when you offer me more tribulation, for as much as you detest me, that much more shall I love you. If this makes you unhappy, that the two of us should end up sharing a single love, then, between the extremes of passion and despair, learn to love or teach me to hate. You will teach me cruelty; I shall teach you generosity. You will teach me bitterness; I shall teach you sweetness. You, disdain; I, love. You, indifference; I, the firmest faith. For it is better, and gives greater glory to love that you should be indifferent for the both of us than that I should love for the both of us.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: Your complaints are so sweet that, although I should like to be swayed by your troubles, I cannot just because you speak them.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: You treat me so badly, from you have I learned the language of despair.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: It is good that you continue, for in such a manner will your eloquent disdain cure your impertinent disposition.

div1.stage: (She begins to leave; Luis stops her.)

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: You have your revenge, now let us both suffer.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: I cannot listen to you more. For God’s sake, cousin, stop him.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: You have so little valor that you should want to hear and see such a thing?

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: Oh, Angela! What am I to do?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Forget Beatriz. To love someone who hates you is not love but death.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: How can I forget her if I still suffer? That is the problem. Tell her to do me a small favor, and I shall forget her with great appreciation. Even the most prudent, the wisest man gives words to his feelings, but I cannot abandon her in my misery. If one can forget a favor more easily, it is because a favor does not sting with the same intensity as an insult.

div1.stage: (Luis leaves the room and enters a patio, where he runs into Rodrigo.)

sp.speaker: Rodrigo
sp.p: What’s going on with you?

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: I have no idea.

sp.speaker: Rodrigo
sp.p: You look so sad. Will you not tell me the cause?

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: I spoke with Beatriz.

sp.speaker: Rodrigo
sp.p: Say no more. I can see in your face how it went. But, where is she? I have not seen her.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: The vixen is a houseguest of my sister for a few days, just so that my problems with guests will be complete. Every day it seems my brother or my sister conspires against me to bring someone else to our house. Whoever they bring, it is bad for me. Manuel..., you know the story. Now with Beatriz, the heavens have decided to bring jealousy into the house as well.

sp.speaker: Rodrigo
sp.p: Careful! Manuel might hear you; here he comes.

p.seg: Am I, alone in all the world, the target of such prodigious misfortune? What shall I do to extract myself from these deceptions? How shall I find out once and for all whether this woman is Luis’s lady, and how she has had the wit and the ability to carry out such intrigues?

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: Manuel.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Luis.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: Where are you coming from in such a good mood?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: The palace.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: I should have known better than to ask a pretender at court about his goings and comings. The palace is clearly the center of your universe.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: If I only went to court, I would be in less of a hurry. But my affairs have taken on a certain urgency. His Majesty has left this afternoon for the palace at Escorial, and now it is of the utmost importance that I follow him.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: If I can be of any assistance, you know that you may count on me.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: I thank you greatly for all you have done for me.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: It is not just a courtesy, I assure you.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: I see you wish me well in my pursuits.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: So true… (Aside) (…and the sooner you leave the better.)

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: But it is not right to take a gentleman such as yourself away from his affairs. I know for a fact that there is something, or someone, of importance to you here. It would be most unfair to take you away.

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: Had you overhead my conversation with Rodrigo, you might think differently.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Am I mistaken?

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: Quite so. Although it is true that I weep on account of the cruelty of a great beauty, her disdain for me causes me as much torment as her favors.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Are you in such despair?

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: I love a great beauty, but without luck or hope of success.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Are you joking?

sp.speaker: Luis
sp.p: I would to heaven that I were. But I was born under such an unlucky star that this beauty flees from me as the veil of night hurries from the lovely light of day, in whose rays I burn. Would you like to know how extreme my misfortune is? Just so that I might not be able to follow her, someone stopped me and kept me from her. Tell me if anyone has worse luck than mine. Most men use go-betweens to help them spend time with their ladies. She uses go-betweens to avoid me.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: What more does he need to declare? A woman who fled from his sight? Another person who interrupted him and kept him from her? He is clearly talking about her and me. At least I have solved part of the puzzle. I now see that she is not his lady, because he would not be so miserable without her if she lived in his own house. But this makes the enigma even greater. If she is not his lady and if she does not live in his house, how then does she write to me? One doubt dies and another is born. What shall I do? This is a confusion of confusions. God protect us from women.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Sir, what has happened to our spook? Have you by any chance seen him around here? As long as I know he is not in our room, I’m happy.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Quiet.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: But I have so much to do in our room, and I can’t enter.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Why not?

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: I’m afraid.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: A man should be afraid?

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: No, he shouldn’t be, but here I am anyway, and for good reason, too.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Please stop your witty remarks, and bring a light, because I have to get ready and write some letters. Tonight I leave Madrid.

sp.speaker: Cosme.
sp.p: That’s interesting. Sounds to me like you’re afraid too.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: I have told you before that I pay no attention to you. I have other things on my mind, and here you are just wasting my time. When I say good-bye to Juan, fetch a lamp.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Indeed I shall, and I’ll shed some light on the ghost, too, and not a moment too soon. There’s bound to be a match around here. I’ll just light up that lamp over there. I’m really on top of things now, if only I could stop shaking with fear.

div1.stage: Enter Isabel through the cupboard with a covered basket.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: They are all out of the house, according to the servant. I have to put this basket of clean linens in the designated place. Heavens! It’s so dark tonight that I’m afraid of my own presence. My God, I’m trembling, and I must be the first spirit ever who swears to God! I cannot find the desk. But what’s this? With my mind in a turmoil and my heart full of fear, I’ve lost my bearing in this room. I have no idea where I am. Where is the table? What am I to do? Oh, no! If I am not able to get out and they find me here, the whole elaborate plan will fall apart. I am greatly afraid, and even more now that I hear someone opening the door. The game is over. I can neither hide nor find my way out.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Oh, spirit, my master, if perhaps my pleas do not fall on the deaf ears of a high-born spook, I humbly beseech you not to remember me in your enchantments. I ask you this for four reasons. (Cosme walks around the stage with Isabel hiding from him by following behind him.) First, I know why; second, you know why; third, everyone knows why; fourth, here’s a poem I just remembered:

lg.l: I am just a young lad,
and hope that safe I’ll be.

p.seg: Now with the light I can reconnoiter the room. He still hasn’t seen me. If I put the light out I know I can escape while he tries to relight it. He may hear some noise, but at least he won’t see me. At this point, I’ll take what I can get.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Fear has made me a pretty good poet!

p.seg: Here we go!

div1.stage: (Isabel strikes Cosme and extinguishes the candle.)

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: My God, she’s killed me. Call a priest! Confession!

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Now’s my chance to escape!

div1.stage: Isabel begins to leave when Manuel enters.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: What is going on here? Cosme, what are you doing here in the darkness?

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: The spirit has killed us both: the light with a puff of air, me with a crushing blow!

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Your fear causes you to imagine things.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Then my imagination will be the death of me!

p.seg: Oh, if only I could find the door!

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Who is there?!

div1.stage: (Isabel bumps into Manuel; he ends grabs the basket of linens.)

p.seg: This is going from bad to worse. Now I run into his master.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Cosme, go get a light. I have the intruder in my grasp.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Don’t let him go!

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: I won’t, but hurry!

p.seg: He took my basket; well, he can have it. There’s the cupboard! At last!

div1.stage: Exit Isabel; Manuel is left holding the basket.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Whoever you are, be still until there is light. If not, by heaven, I shall have to run you through with my dagger. But, there is nothing here but something lightweight, something with linens in it. What on earth? My God, I have never been so confused!

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Let’s see this phantom in the light! But, where is he? Didn’t you have him captive? What happened? Where is he? Sir, what in the devil is going on?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: I cannot answer. He left me these linens, then fled.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: And what do you make of this situation? You just now said that you had him in control, and he vanished!

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: I must admit that that person, who enters and leaves with extraordinary guile and cunning, was in fact captured here tonight. But, in order to escape, he blew out your light, left me with this basket, and fled.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: How?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Through the door.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: You are driving me mad. I saw him in the dying light of my candle.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: What did he look like?

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: He was a little, bitty monk, wearing a great big hood. That’s why I think our spook must be a Capuchin friar.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: The things fear drives one to! Bring the light. Let’s see what our little friar left us. Here, hold this basket.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: You want me to hold this basket from hell?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Just be quiet and hold it.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: My hands are dirty, Sir, from the candle wax. I’ll surly soil the fine linen that covers it. Perhaps you should put it on the floor!

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: It’s fresh linens… and a note! Let’s see if our friar is discreet: (Reads) “In the brief time that you have lived in this house, no one has yet brought you fresh linens. As they are made ready, they will be brought to you. Regarding your supposition about your friend, since you are sure that I am Luis’s lady, I can assure you that not only am I not his lady, but that I cannot be. I leave the rest for when we meet, which will be soon. God be with you.” Well, at least the spirit is a Christian, since he speaks of God!

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: You see? A religious spirit!

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: It’s getting late. Collect all these suitcases and cushions, and put these papers with them (He gives him some papers). They are the reason we are here at court. But first I intend to send an answer to our spirit.

div1.stage: (Cosme puts the papers on a chair; Manuel writes.)

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: I’ll put them right here so that I won’t forget them and they’ll be right at hand. But I have to rest a moment. Tell me one thing: do you believe in ghosts?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: What foolishness!

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Foolishness? You yourself can see the effects. You’re sitting there with a letter that came to you out of nowhere, and still you doubt? Fine, if that makes you happy. As for me, I’m a believer; I’ve suffered the most,

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: How so?

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Just look at us. If they rifle through our clothing, you laugh at the intrusion, but I have to repack everything, which is no small job. If they leave you papers, you’re impressed by the wit. Me, they leave coals and take my money. If they bring you sweets, you’re as pleased as a father to accept them. I get nothing, and I’m hungry as a wolf. They give you fine shirts and handkerchiefs of linen. I get nothing but scary surprises. We both came to this room at about the same time, but you get a basket of clean linens, smelling as sweet as springtime. I get a slap in the face, a blow so hard and strong that I practically spit up my brains. All the pleasure and the profit go to you; the pain and suffering are all mine. The ghost treats you with kid gloves; I get the brass knuckles. So just let me believe what I will. There is nothing more painful to watch than a man who won’t believe what’s happening right before his eyes.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Just pack the suitcases, so we may go. I shall wait for you in Juan’s room

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: What is there to pack? Everyone dresses in black, just as you are already. All you need is a black cloak.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Leave the room locked and take the key with you. If I need the key, Juan has another one. I hate to leave in such confusion, not knowing the truth of the matter. But the honor of my estate and my chances at court take precedence over an idle curiosity. Indeed, honor trumps everything else.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: It happened just like that?

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: I saw the whole artifice going up in flames. If he had seen me, it would have been necessary to confess everything. As it turned out, I was able to escape in the manner I just related.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Amazing!

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: It is simply incredible to think that you could give a man a basket of linens without his seeing you!

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: If after all this I am able to arrange for him to see me as we planned, I have no doubt that he will surely lose his mind.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: Even the most serious person would be astonished by these goings-on, Angela. You want to call him to a place without telling him where so that he can find himself with a beautiful lady, rich and famous, without knowing who she is or where she is from. Then, cloaked and blind, he is to be led away to stew in his confusion. This is what comes out of that head of yours? I am in awe!

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Everything is just as you said. But since you are here with me, tonight will not be the night of our meeting.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: I can keep the secret of your love!

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: No, cousin, that’s not the reason. With you in our house, and with my brothers buzzing about you hopelessly in love, idolizing the very ground you walk on, it would be entirely too risky. I’ll have to wait until they leave.

div1.stage: (Enter Luis, who eavesdrops from the side of the stage.)

p.seg: Good God! Who can suppress his desires? Who can rein in his thoughts, control his tongue, and imprison his feelings? Since I am beside myself, surely I cannot. But let me try to conquer my passion. I shall just watch from here.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: Let me tell you how to get rid of them but still let me be present. I would hate to miss the conclusion of this marvelous adventure.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Do tell me!

p.seg: What are these two scheming? My heart is in my throat with anticipation.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: We shall both say that my father has sent for me, and we shall make a great show of my leaving, but secretly I shall hide in the house and no one will know I am here.

p.seg: Heavens, what is this that threatens the honor of this house?

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: Under the cover of secrecy, I shall be able to see what happens.

p.seg: Oh, cruel fortune!

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: I look so forward to it!

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: But what do we say in order to bring you out of hiding?

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: I am shocked you would ask! No doubt we can think of something later!

p.seg: No doubt. That I should have to listen to this! The torment and suffering surpass all limits.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: This way, in secret and with no witnesses, I shall see you fulfill your love. With me hidden and the household unsuspecting, he will have no trouble passing from his room to yours.

p.seg: It is easy to infer her intention. What a coward I am! I am undone! Would that I had never listened! My fortunate brother deserves Beatriz more. But what jealousy! She prefers to offer herself to him and thus quench both their desires. Thus she arranges for him to pass from his room to hers without anyone noticing. I can scarcely contain my anger! And so that no one might be a witness they succeed in making real my suspicions. My enemies want to keep the secret from me! By God, if that is the way it is, I shall not allow it. The next time that she is hidden, hoping for another meeting, I shall keep close watch over the entire house until I find her. The fires of jealousy that consume me allow for no alternative. Placing obstacles in their way is the last refuge of the jealous man. Holy saints protect me! Consumed by love, I’m dying of jealousy.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Everything is set up. Tomorrow we shall announce your departure.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: Angela! And the lovely Beatriz!

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: Just the man we were hoping to see.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: If my absence causes you to enjoy my presence even more, then may you miss me more often, madam. I am suspicious, no, envious, of my own good luck. It is simply not possible that I deserve your affection. Envious and envied, I fall into such a sweet abyss that I both envy and pity myself.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: It would not be right to contradict such sweet arguments, Juan, from one who has put off seeing me for so long as to have forgotten me. Is there any doubt that you were engaged in your own amusements? It must be so, for you profess both to envy and pity your good fortune, while at the same time you cast aside the beauty that gives you such pleasure. Your clear and convincing syllogism proves your pity and your envy.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: If it would not offend both you and me, Beatriz, I would tell you that I have been with my guest, Manuel, who has left us tonight.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Really?

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: You are surprised, sister?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: A pleasure startles as much as a displeasure.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: I regret that your heart’s desire has not been fulfilled; he will return tomorrow.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: (Aside.) A vain hope is revived. — I was not afraid on account of his leaving. His comings and goings are always inopportune.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: I did not think that you were. It is just that you and Luis show nothing but displeasure at the visit of this friend that causes me such pleasure.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: I do not know how to answer you, although I feel as though I must. I think I should retire from your game of love. Three’s company, and you have made of me a go-between, when love is most enjoyable when played as a two-handed game, one on one. Isabel, come with me. — (Aside) This very night shall we retrieve the portrait. We shall have more time and fewer interruptions. Bring me a light and show me where to hide. A man who writes me letters has no business possessing the portrait of another lady. The insult!

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: I do not believe that I owe you such kindness.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: I shall prove the strength of my commitment —which is substantial— with words.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: Please do.

sp.speaker: Juan
sp.p: Listen, my love. Beautiful Beatriz, my faith is so certain, my love so steadfast, my affection so extraordinary, that even if I did not wish to love you, against my own will and desire would I love you still. My life now depends upon yours so much that if I could forget you, I would, just so that I might fall in love with you all over again. Would that I could experience again the happy, mad rush of new love. He who loves a woman only when he cannot forget her, does not oblige her to love him in return, since without the possibility of choice determined by free will, it cannot be called love. Yet I cannot possibly get your beauty out of my mind, Beatriz, and I am left to despair that the stars swell with pride at the victory of your love over my free will.

sp.speaker: Beatriz
sp.p: If choices were due to free will, and forces to the influence of the stars, she who lives not subject to fortune would have a stronger will than mine. I cannot trust your kindness since my faith, which can overcome impossible obstacles, would deny that it were my own if my will were not accompanied by it. During that brief instant spent in forgetting you so that I might fall in love with you again, my heart would feel my life slipping away. I am delighted to have no part in putting you out of my mind since I could not love you while I tried to forget you.

div1.stage: (Enter Manuel, chasing Cosme, who is trying to flee.)

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: For God’s sake, if I had seen…

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: That’s why you look.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: …that your incompetence was going to dishonor me, to make a fool of me!

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: You know that I have served you well. Things happen, even to good Catholic servants!

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: You are hopeless. The one thing that mattered most to me, the one thing I entrusted to your safe-keeping, is the one thing that you forgot.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: That’s why I forgot it, because it was so important to me. If it weren’t so important, why would I bother to forget it? I swear, I was so careful to collect all those papers and set them aside. It was my care and attention that caused you all this misery. If I hadn’t set them aside, I would have gathered them up with the rest.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: At least you remembered them… when we were half-way there!

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: I was very worried. I knew something was wrong. I thought it was probably nothing until I remembered that I forgot the papers.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Tell the groom to wait with the horses. I do not wish to make a noisy entrance, waking up the entire household that is surely asleep. Entering is no problem, since I have the key. I should be able to retrieve my papers without troubling a soul.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: I already told the groom to wait. But look, sir, it’s a real mistake to try to find those papers without light. There’s just no way to keep from making noise. If we can’t find a candle or a lamp, how shall we see?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Is there no end to the problems you cause? What, now you want me to call out and wake the whole house? Do you not realize that you are to blame for all this? Where exactly did you leave the papers?

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: That’s no problem. I know exactly where I left them once we get in the room. I can find them in the dark.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Go on in.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: What I don’t know is what that spook may have done with them. So far nothing I have set down has been in the same place when I went back for it.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: If they are not there, then we shall ask for a light. Until we know for sure, it is better to move quickly and, above all, quietly. I would hate to disturb our gracious hosts.

div1.stage: (Angela and Isabel enter through the cupboard.)

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Isabel, the house is now asleep and everything is as it should be. Our guest has left, so now is the time to retrieve the portrait he had the very first time I saw him.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Enter quietly. Be very careful.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Go back through and lock the door to my room. In order not to create a stir, I shall not move until you get back..

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Wait right here.

div1.stage: (Exit Isabel, who closes the cupboard. Enter Manuel and Cosme.)

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: It’s open.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Walk softly. If they hear us, it will cause quite a scandal.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: I hope you believe me now when I tell you I’m afraid. The ghost could at least have brought us a light.

p.seg: Good thing I brought this lantern under my cloak so that no one could see it.

div1.stage: (With Angela on one side of the room and Manuel and Cosme on the other, Angela brings out a lantern that she had hidden under her cloak.)

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: This is the most accommodating goblin I’ve ever heard tell of. Look how quickly it brings us a light! You’ll notice that the ghost likes you… he produces a light when you need it. When I had one, he snuffed it out.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Good heavens! This is unnatural and quite extraordinary. To have produced a light so quickly is not human.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: You see? I told you you’d end up believing me.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: I am frozen with fear. We must go back.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: At least now we know you’re mortal since you finally showed fear.

p.seg: Here is the table, covered with papers.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: The ghost is going toward the table.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: My God, I both doubt and believe what my eyes perceive.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Look! It’s guiding us exactly to the things we are looking for. I wish we could see who’s carrying the light.

div1.stage: (Angela removes the candle from the lantern and puts it in a candle holder on the table. She takes a chair and sits with her back to the two men.)

p.seg: I shall place the light here so I might see the desk.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Wait. I can see everything by the light of that candle. I have never in my life seen a lady so beautiful. My heavens! What is this that to my eyes appears? Her charms are like the hydra: each one gives rise to a thousand more. What shall I do?

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: She’s moving slowly. She’s drawing up a chair.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: She is the very image of the rarest beauty that the brush of the Almighty has ever produced.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: True enough. She is His creation.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Her eyes shine more brightly than lamplight.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: No doubt because her eyes are the stars in Lucifer’s sky.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Her tresses are rays of the sun.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: She probably stole them from it.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Each curl is a star.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: If you say so. Just remember, supernatural forces brought her here.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: I have never seen such loveliness.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: You wouldn’t say that if you could see her feet. They say that you can tell the devil by his feet.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: She is a beautiful angel, a paragon of splendor.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Still, I’d like to take a gander at those hooves.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Wait. What is she doing with my papers?

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: My guess is that she wants to see the very ones we have come back for. That way we will have less to do. She is a very accommodating spirit.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Heaven help me! I know not what to do! I have never before felt like such a coward.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Boy, I have!

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: My feet are imprisoned in chains of ice. My every breath is like a dagger in my chest and a rope around my neck. But why am I afraid? By God, I must attempt to break free of this enchantment. (He approaches Angela and grabs her.) Angel, demon, or woman! You shall not escape my grasp this time.

p.seg: Oh, unhappy me! He had not really left the house. He has the advantage here.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: In the name of God (who brings the devil to his knees), tell us…

p.seg: I must continue my deception.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: …who are you, and what do you want from us?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Most generous Manuel Enríquez, for whom great good fortune lies in wait, touch me not, approach me not, or you will lose the greatest gift that heaven has in store for you. Fate has decreed that you should receive a great reward. I wrote to you this afternoon, in my last letter, and told you that we should see each other soon, and so it has come to pass. I have fulfilled my promise, since you see me here now in the most human form that I can manage. So go now, leave me here in peace. The time is not yet right for you to know and understand the truth of my situation. All will be revealed tomorrow. But you must tell no one of our meeting lest you lose the greatest blessing imaginable. Go in peace.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Since she invites us so peaceably, what are we waiting for?

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: (Aside) God in heaven! I have had enough of fearing empty shadows! Since my courage will not stand for any more confusion, I must clear up the mystery. — Woman, whoever you may be, I shall never believe that you are anything else. But by God I shall know who you are, how you have entered here, for what end, everything! And I shall have the truth long before tomorrow. Woman or devil, I must persist. If you are a devil, your threats no longer daunt me. But of course I know by your form that you are not a devil but a woman.

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Is there a difference?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Touch me not, or you will lose a great deal. play

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: The devil’s right. She’s not a harp or a lute or a drum that will respond to your touch.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: I shall see now by my sword whether or not you are a spirit. Even if should wound you, it should not hurt you.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: No! Hold your sword, restrain your bloodthirsty arm. It is not right that you should kill a wretched woman. I confess that that is what I am. Although love is a crime, I do not deserve dying miserably just for loving well. Sully not with my blood the brilliant steel of your sword.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Who are you?

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: I must tell you. I cannot fulfill this love, this desire, this truth, and this faith, as I hoped. But we are in danger of death if they see us or hear us. There is much more to me than you see here. Thus it is necessary, in order to remove what obstacles may be, to lock that door, sir, and the outer door as well, so that no one passing by may see our light.

sp.speaker: Manuel
sp.p: Light the candle, Cosme, and let’s close these doors. You see that she is a woman and not a ghost?

sp.speaker: Cosme
sp.p: Just as I said all along.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: Heavens! Now I am locked in this room. I suppose I shall have to tell him the truth since Isabel has left me here alone and the guest has caught me.

sp.speaker: Isabel
sp.p: Psst! Madam! Your brother is asking for you.

sp.speaker: Angela
sp.p: What luck! Open the other side of the cupboard. Ah, my love, you will have to live with your doubts a bit longer.

div1.stage: (Exeunt, closing the cupboard as they leave. Enter Manuel and Cosme.)

sp.speaker: Manuel
